eventMetadata.context_description: **Traders have converged on 33°C as the near-certain highest temperature in Ankara on August 3, 2026, reflecting the latest consensus from official forecasts.** The Turkish State Meteorological Service (MGM) and international models such as those feeding AccuWeather and BBC outlooks consistently project a daytime maximum near this level under stable summer high-pressure conditions typical for early August in central Anatolia. Current observational trends show no significant deviation from seasonal norms, with limited cloud cover and light northerly winds expected to moderate any local heating. Historical climatology places early-August highs around 30–32°C on average, and the absence of anomalous atmospheric patterns or incoming frontal systems supports the tight clustering around 33°C. A realistic challenge would require an unforecasted rapid shift, such as stronger-than-expected advection of cooler air or localized convective cooling, though model agreement remains high with little divergence noted in recent runs.

**Trader consensus has coalesced on 37°C as the implied probability outcome for Taipei’s highest temperature on August 3, 2026, reflecting near-certainty based on real-time Central Weather Administration (CWA) observations and model guidance.** 

Summer conditions in northern Taiwan typically produce daytime highs of 32–36°C under subtropical high pressure, with heat indices amplified by humidity. Recent model runs and surface observations indicate peak readings reaching or touching 37°C (approximately 99°F) at official stations such as Songshan, consistent with the CWA’s “extremely hot” advisory for the day. Historical August maxima in Taipei frequently approach or exceed this threshold when steering patterns allow prolonged solar heating and limited cloud cover. 

The market’s strong positioning rests on the alignment of multiple forecast cycles and preliminary station data showing afternoon temperatures climbing into the upper 30s Celsius. Only an unexpected late-day cooling from convective showers or a measurement revision below the 37°C threshold—both low-probability events given current conditions—could alter the outcome before official daily records close.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus has converged at 100% implied probability on a 31°C high for Guangzhou on August 3, 2026, driven by official observations confirming that peak under persistent cloud cover and rain.** 

August climatology in this subtropical monsoon region typically produces highs of 32–34°C, yet reduced solar insolation from widespread precipitation and high humidity suppressed temperatures. China Meteorological Administration ensemble forecasts clustered tightly around 29–31°C, with minimal model spread and no breaks in the cloud deck to allow stronger heating. Historical analogs show similar rainy-day maxima in early August rarely exceed 31°C when daily rainfall totals reach several millimeters. 

Realistic challenges remain limited to post-event data revisions from primary stations or shifts in resolution criteria, though current verified measurements make such outcomes highly improbable.

Historical August baselines for the region average around 33°C, and current steering patterns plus humidity levels align with this range. A sudden clearing of cloud cover or delayed rainfall could allow brief spikes above 34°C, though model consensus and ongoing precipitation make such shifts improbable before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Ongoing heat wave conditions across Shandong province, reinforced by an official High Temperature Orange Warning issued August 1, 2026, position 34–35 °C as the most probable peak for Qingdao on August 5.** The Shandong Meteorological Observatory forecast calls for maximum temperatures of 37–39 °C (with localized pockets possibly exceeding 40 °C) from August 2–5 in northern Qingdao and adjacent inland areas, while other districts are expected to reach 34–36 °C. This extended episode follows record readings of 40.8 °C elsewhere in the province on August 1 and aligns with broader seasonal patterns of above-average summer heat and high humidity (50–80 % RH) driven by monsoon influences.

Coastal Qingdao’s marine moderation and typical August climatology (long-term daytime maxima near 29–30 °C) introduce downward pressure, tempering the risk of extreme outliers above 36 °C. Short-range model consensus and recent station observations support the market’s clustering around 34–35 °C (71 % combined probability), with the 22 % chance assigned to 36 °C+ reflecting residual uncertainty in localized inland heating and any last-minute forecast revisions ahead of the August 5 observation window.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Cape Town International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Cape Town International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/za/matroosfontein/FACT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.
